name: ESP32-DevKitC V4 (38 pin)
description: Espressif reference ESP32 board, 38 pins with the flash pins brought out. 3.3 V logic, USB powered.
notes: All GPIO are 3.3 V only (absolute max 3.6 V). A 5 V signal (HC-SR04 ECHO, 5 V Arduino) needs a level shifter or divider.
Strapping pins GPIO0, GPIO2, GPIO5, GPIO12 and GPIO15 set the boot mode. Do not pull GPIO12 high or GPIO0 low at reset, and avoid parts that drive these pins during power-up.
GPIO34, GPIO35, GPIO36 (VP) and GPIO39 (VN) are input only and have no internal pull-ups.
ADC2 pins (GPIO0, 2, 4, 12-15, 25-27) cannot be read while WiFi is on: use ADC1 (GPIO32-39) for analog.
Recommended per-pin current about 20 mA, absolute 40 mA. Do not power servos or motors from the 3V3 pin.

Current draw: about 80-120 mA average with WiFi on, short bursts of about 250-350 mA during transmit and boot (modelled as current_peak 0.35 A). Espressif recommends a supply that can give at least 500 mA, so a laptop USB port is just enough for the board plus small sensors.
Pin order per the Espressif DevKitC V4 header tables J2 (left, antenna up) and J3 (right). Many generic 38-pin boards copy this order, but check the silkscreen.
SD2, SD3, CMD, CLK, SD0, SD1 (GPIO6-11) go to the SPI flash: never connect anything to them.
Power: USB, or regulated 5 V on the 5V pin, or 3.3 V on 3V3. Use only one at a time.
Breadboard: the header rows are 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) apart, so on a standard breadboard it covers every hole on one side. Use two breadboards side by side or jumpers to a separate board.

pins.label: 3V3
pins.note: Output of the onboard 3.3 V LDO (about 0.4 A left for external parts). Can also feed the board from a 3.3 V supply if 5V and USB are unpowered.

pins.label: EN
pins.note: Chip enable / reset, pulled up on the board.
